Dmitry Vladimirovich, it is time for you to go home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Ребята, ну ладно, простите меня, я был не прав.
examples.trans: Guys, come on, forgive me, I was wrong.
Yes, Vika, forgive me, I got swamped.
Lena, forgive me, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Моя камбала там не постарела, а?
examples.trans: Hasn't my flounder grown old over there, huh?
Fedya, can you go faster?

examples.text: Нетерпеливый! Девушки просят меня быть помедленнее.
examples.trans: Impatient! Girls ask me to go more slowly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: You're welcome, Max.
Here you are, please.
Lena, forgive me, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не раздражает поваров больше, чем официанты.
examples.trans: Nobody irritates cooks more than waiters.
Fedya, can you go faster?
You have really gotten on everyone's nerves already.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'saw', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: Have you seen my little elephant?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Champagne for everyone on my tab!
Dima, you should go home.

examples.text: А где мой завтрак? Вот мой завтрак!
examples.trans: And where is my breakfast? Here is my breakfast!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лоник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'little elephant figurine' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А почему ты слоника не носишь, который я тебе подарила?
examples.trans: And why aren't you carrying the little elephant that I gave you?
You gave me that wretched elephant.

examples.text: Лена, ну не ты виновата, а слон этот, которого я потерял!
examples.trans: Lena, well you aren't to blame, it's that elephant that I lost!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Хотел тебя предупредить, мы завтра идём в кино.
examples.trans: I wanted to let you know, tomorrow we are going to the cinema.

examples.text: Вика, я хотел с тобой поговорить.
examples.trans: Vika, I wanted to talk with you.

examples.text: Я просто хотел сказать, что мне вчера показалось...
examples.trans: I just wanted to say that yesterday it seemed to me...

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They are unceremonious.

examples.text: Моя камбала там не постарела, а?
examples.trans: Hasn't my flounder grown old over there, huh?

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Вика, я хотел с тобой поговорить.
examples.trans: Vika, I wanted to talk with you.

examples.text: Давай я приеду, мы обо всём поговорим.
examples.trans: Let me come over, we will talk about everything.

examples.text: Хорошо, придёшь в себя — мы поговорим.
examples.trans: Fine, when you come to your senses, we will talk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А я виноват, что вы такие криворукие?
examples.trans: Am I to blame that you are so clumsy?
Ilyusha, prepare something festive for me.
And why have you crowded around here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф, это не ерунда, это большая игра.
examples.trans: Chef, this is not nonsense, this is a big game.
This is a big game!

examples.text: И это солидные деньги? Марш работать!
examples.trans: And that is serious money? March back to work!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'prank' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What is this? Some kind of prank, huh?

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть розыгрыш.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always prank.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is this? Some kind of prank, huh?
What nonsense.
Some man called you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не раздражает поваров больше, чем официанты.
examples.trans: Nobody irritates cooks more than waiters.

examples.text: Моя камбала там не постарела, а?
examples.trans: Hasn't my flounder grown old over there, huh?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'волочь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'scoundrels, bastards' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сволочи! А кого я накажу, а?
examples.trans: Scoundrels! And who am I going to punish, huh?
Ah, you bastard!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'whom', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не раздражает поваров больше, чем официанты.
examples.trans: Nobody irritates cooks more than waiters.

examples.text: Молодец! А кому премия, Виктория Сергеевна?
examples.trans: Well done! And who gets a bonus, Viktoria Sergeyevna?
Did someone die? No.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will punish', paired with 'наказывать'.

examples.trans: History will punish them.
Mum will punish him.
To punish the blind?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Какие три тысячи? Ты же сказал подарок!
examples.trans: What three thousand? You said it was a gift!

examples.text: Я просто хотел сказать, что мне вчера показалось...
examples.trans: I just wanted to say that yesterday it seemed to me...
So you mean to say...

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.text: Вика, ты мне хоть скажи, что происходит здесь?
examples.trans: Vika, at least tell me what is going on here?
What is going on? I don't understand.
What is happening here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я её год ищу, а она здесь валяется.
examples.trans: I have been looking for it for a year, and it is lying around here.

examples.text: Вика, ты мне хоть скажи, что происходит здесь?
examples.trans: Vika, at least tell me what is going on here?
I'm here.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('only, sole').

examples.trans: The only reasonable person!
The only chance.
This performance is our only chance!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('reasonable, sane').

examples.trans: The only reasonable person!

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень адекватный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very reasonable choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'man' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А то человек есть, а блюда нет.
examples.trans: Otherwise the person is here, and the dish is not.
About fifteen people.
The only reasonable person!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who, which (relative)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Небрежный. Хуже только официант, который был поваром.
examples.trans: Careless. Worse is only a waiter who used to be a cook.

examples.text: А почему ты слоника не носишь, который я тебе подарила?
examples.trans: And why aren't you carrying the little elephant that I gave you?

examples.text: Твоя задача какая? Следить за едой, которую ты мне подаёшь.
examples.trans: What is your job? To watch over the food that you serve me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'never', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Who never stole.
Never betrayed me.
Never secretly fried my zucchini.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'ровать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stole', paired with 'своровать'.

examples.trans: Who never stole.
I am not going to steal a dog.
Stealing is bad.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'авать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'betrayed', paired with 'предать'.

examples.trans: Never betrayed me.

examples.text: А ты сейчас свою семью предаёшь!
examples.trans: And you are betraying your family right now!

examples.text: И если бы не предавал своих друзей.
examples.trans: And if he had not betrayed his friends.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'zucchini' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Never secretly fried my zucchini.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть кабачок.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always zucchini.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'fried', paired with 'пожарить'.

examples.trans: Never secretly fried my zucchini.

examples.text: Повар жарит сочное мясо на сковороде.
examples.trans: The cook fries juicy meat on the pan.

examples.text: Нет, Федя сам жарил эту куропатку!
examples.trans: No, Fedya roasted that partridge himself!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful').

examples.trans: You are unattractive. Come here.
Unattractive guy, go work.
So beautiful.

examples.trans: Right, I will go arrange champagne for the guests.

examples.text: А что тогда не идёшь? Спартак же играет!
examples.trans: Then why aren't you going? Spartak is playing!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'it's time', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: О, грибы! Мне один дурак на корпоративе дал.
examples.trans: Oh, mushrooms! Some fool gave them to me at an office party.
Chef, are you all right?
It is time for me to work.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Виктория Сергеевна, душа моя! А чего не дома?
examples.trans: Viktoria Sergeyevna, my soul! Why aren't you at home?
Dima, you should go home.

examples.text: Я и так у себя дома.
examples.trans: I am already at home.
